inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report consolidated cash flow statement, 'Share-based payments' add-back HK$6,790k (0467.HK_Annual_FY2025.txt:3102). No net-share-settlement tax line; equity-award taxes nil.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T08:08:06Z regular close (HKEX), Yahoo Finance chart API
inputs.share_count_basis: 25,679.6m shares in issue at 30 June 2026 (H1 FY2026 interim; weighted average for EPS). The company reports no dilutive securities (diluted EPS 'N/A', H1-2026 note 10(b)). Held flat: SBC is expensed in the flows (and immaterial at ~HK$7m/yr). No buybacks in FY2025 or H1 FY2026, so the flat count is a convention the company is not actively funding, though SBC is too small for this to matter.
inputs.revenue_basis: base_revenue is FY2025 turnover EXCLUDING the Trading segment: Exploration & production HK$9,429.3m + Clean energy HK$173.8m = HK$9,603.1m (FY2025 AR turnover table, line 627-638). Trading (HK$9,588m FY2025, HK$6,067m H1 FY2026) is third-party crude/product cargo trading around the Group's Iraq/Pakistan liftings and earns roughly nil (segment loss HK$10.6m in H1 FY2026, HK$8.8m in H1 FY2025). Including it would halve every margin and let trading volume, not oil economics, drive growth. Its working capital is carried inside the wc_capture driver. E&P turnover is already net of royalty, windfall levy and PSC government take.
inputs.wacc_rationale: HKD flows; the HKD is pegged to the USD so the rate is built USD-style. Risk-free ~4.2% (10y UST/HK govt), ERP 5.5%, levered beta ~1.2 for a small-cap E&P, plus a ~2.5pp country-risk premium because >95% of production sits in Iraq (Block 9, ~50% of WI output), Pakistan and Egypt, all sub-investment-grade sovereigns with state counterparties (Basra Oil Company, SSGC, EGPC). Cost of equity ~13.3%. Pre-tax cost of debt 9.9% (H1 FY2026 weighted average, all USD), small weight (borrowings ~23% of market cap). WACC ~12% all scenarios. Country/sovereign risk is charged in the rate; commodity price and volume risk are charged in the scenario flows. No per-scenario WACC differences (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt: EBITDA is post-IFRS 16 so lease payments are not in the flows; lease liabilities of HK$274.1m at 30 June 2026 are included in total_debt / net_debt. Lease principal (HK$148.7m FY2025) is not deducted from flows.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI is HK$5.4m of equity (immaterial); ignored in both flows and bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: Owner-FCF DCF with the non-US/cyclical adaptations (dcf-methods routing row 'Operating company, non-US or cyclical'). United Energy is an operating upstream oil & gas producer (Pakistan gas/condensate, Iraq Block 9 and Siba oil/gas, Egypt Western Desert oil incl. Apex acquired 14-Oct-2025) plus a small wind/solar business; it is not a bank, REIT, holdco or distressed shell, so the FCF engine applies. First valuation of this ticker (no MEMORY.md entry, no prior DCF). NET DEBT at 30 June 2026: borrowings HK$3,326.8m (749.3 current + 2,577.5 non-current) + lease liabilities HK$274.1m - cash HK$3,368.1m = HK$232.8m. Decommissioning provision HK$751.6m deducted in the equity bridge (a debt-like abandonment obligation not in the flows). INTEREST INCOME (HK$87m FY2025) not stripped: the Group is roughly net-debt-neutral, so there is no cash pile counted twice; interest received is classified in investing, outside reported FCF. SBC-ZERO MARKET in substance (SBC 0.07% of revenue): house and street bases are effectively identical; band_position is degenerate and should be read as n/a. CYCLICALITY: FY2026 is a high-price year (H1 realised crude US$78.76/bbl vs US$68.19 in H1 FY2025, driven by the Hormuz disruption), partly offset by BOC curtailments in Iraq that were lifted in June 2026. The base path takes FY2026 at elevated margin and normalises to a ~US$65 Brent mid-cycle margin from FY2027. Capex FY2026 follows guidance (US$500-600m, managed to the lower end, ~HK$4.0bn = ~40% of ex-trading revenue), then reverts toward D&A (~47-48%) because sustaining reserves at a ~16-year WI 2P life (679.6 mmboe at YE2025) requires capex roughly equal to depletion. CONCENTRATION: Iraq Block 9 (60% WI, operator) is ~half of WI production and exports depend on the Strait of Hormuz; five largest customers were 81.7% of FY2025 turnover. DIVIDEND: FY2025 dividends paid HK$1,292m exceeded owner FCF of HK$894m (funded by the US$-denominated borrowings drawn for Apex), so the ~12% trailing yield is not covered at mid-cycle prices. NO-RE-RATE MEMO: the stock trades at ~1.7x EV/FY2025 EBITDA and ~10x trailing earnings; the 5-6x FCF exit caps below are deliberately close to what the market already pays rather than assuming a re-rating.

equity_bridge.note: H1 FY2026 interim note 17, balance at 30 June 2026 (HK$751,641k); debt-like abandonment obligation not in the projected flows

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (0.4% 5y, -5.9% 3y) diverges by far more than 30% from reported revenue CAGR (25.3% 5y). Reported revenue growth is inflated by the low-margin Trading segment (nil in early years, HK$9.6bn in FY2025) and by the FY2022 oil-price spike; ex-trading E&P turnover fell from HK$10.1bn (FY2024) to HK$9.4bn (FY2025). Equity has gone sideways because dividends (~HK$1.0-1.3bn/yr) absorb most earnings and FY2023 carried a large impairment (net loss HK$1.7bn). Equity CAGR is the better guide: this is a no-growth, high-payout, depleting-asset business.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs computed on annual rows of Metrics.csv: revenue FY2022->FY2025 (3y) and FY2020->FY2025 (5y), likewise EPS, equity and owner FCF (reported FCF - SBC; interest income not stripped because net cash is immaterial). The 5y owner-FCF CAGR is meaningless (FY2020 base HK$16.8m in the COVID oil collapse) and is left null. SBC is immaterial (HK$7-18m/yr), so the owner-FCF and reported-FCF CAGRs are essentially identical; SBC is not funding growth.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026: H1 ex-trading turnover HK$4,871m (+9% YoY) on high realised prices despite Iraq curtailment; H2 gets restored Iraq liftings and a full half of Apex but lower prices -> FY2026 ~HK$10.1bn (+5%). FY2027 -6% as Brent normalises to ~US$65. Thereafter roughly flat volumes: Egypt growth and Iraq plateau offset Pakistan gas decline (Pakistan Energy Outlook: domestic gas output falling ~5%/yr).
base.ebitda_margin_rationale: FY2025 EBITDA HK$6,446m on ex-trading revenue = 67% at US$69 Brent; FY2024 73% at US$81; H1 FY2026 75.6% at US$79 realised crude. FY2026 72% (high H1, normalising H2); 66% mid-cycle thereafter (opex ~US$4.9/boe is low, so margin is mostly price-driven).
base.capex_rationale: FY2026 guidance US$500-600m, managed to the lower end (~HK$4.0bn, 41%). FY2022-25 capex averaged ~55% of ex-trading revenue; long-run 48%, about equal to D&A, i.e. sustaining production and reserves rather than growing them.
base.da_rationale: D&A FY2025 HK$4,756m = 50% of ex-trading revenue; FY2024 53%. Slightly lower going forward as capex is cut; matters only for cash tax.
base.cash_tax_rationale: Cash taxes paid / (EBITDA - D&A): FY2025 765/1,690 = 45%; FY2024 950/2,082 = 46%; FY2022-23 8-13% (on a different D&A base). Pakistan corporate tax plus super tax on a group EBIT depressed by full-field DD&A. 40% used.
base.wc_rationale: Negative capture: receivables from state buyers (Pakistan circular debt at SSGC, EGPC in Egypt, BOC lifting arrangements) and trading working capital consume cash as revenue grows and release it as revenue falls.

scenario_narratives.base: Brent settles near US$65 after the 2026 Hormuz spike; Iraq Block 9 liftings run at pre-conflict levels, Egypt (with Apex) grows modestly and offsets Pakistan's gas decline, so working-interest output holds around 105-115k boed. Capex reverts from the FY2026 squeeze to roughly D&A to keep the ~16-year 2P reserve life intact. Owner FCF settles near HK$1.0bn a year -- roughly FY2025's HK$0.9bn -- which does not cover the current ~HK$1.3bn dividend; the payout is trimmed or debt-funded. Exit at 6x FCF reflects a depleting asset in frontier jurisdictions.
scenario_narratives.bull: Brent holds US$70-75, Egypt's exploration hits (3 discoveries in H1 FY2026) and the Apex integration lift volumes, Pakistan discoveries slow the gas decline, and Iraq expands beyond plateau. Margin stays near FY2024's ~70%, capex runs below D&A as recent discoveries are developed cheaply, and the market grants a 7x FCF exit as reserve replacement proves out.
scenario_narratives.bear: Oil falls to ~US$55 as the post-Hormuz supply surge (OPEC+ +3 mmbbld in June 2026) meets weaker demand; renewed Gulf conflict or a BOC dispute curtails Iraq again; Pakistan circular debt stretches receivables and gas output declines ~5%/yr; Egypt EGPC payment delays recur. Revenue steps down 15% in FY2027 and keeps declining ~3%/yr as reserves deplete faster than capex replaces them; margin compresses to the high 50s while capex stays at half of revenue. Exit at 5x with negative terminal growth: a run-off.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 30% from the 15% default: production is concentrated in one Iraqi block whose exports pass through Hormuz (curtailed in H1 FY2026), all buyers are sovereign or state-linked counterparties in sub-investment-grade countries, and oil is the dominant price driver. Base 50%: FY2026 guidance and the June 2026 lifting of Iraq curtailments support a mid-cycle path. Bull cut to 20% because it needs both higher oil and successful reserve replacement in Egypt/Pakistan at the same time.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value a depleting, high-payout upstream producer on mid-cycle owner FCF. Revenue excludes zero-margin trading, capex is held near D&A so the model pays to sustain reserves, sovereign/country risk sits in a 12% HKD WACC, and commodity and volume risk sit in the bear-weighted scenarios. The exit multiples (5-7x FCF) are close to what the stock already trades on; no re-rating is assumed.
key_risks_to_valuation: Oil price: margin is mostly price-driven (opex ~US$4.9/boe); each US$10/bbl moves EBITDA by roughly HK$1.5-2bn
Iraq Block 9 concentration (~50% of WI production) and Strait of Hormuz export dependence; BOC curtailments in H1 FY2026
Sovereign counterparty credit: Pakistan circular debt (SSGC), EGPC receivables in Egypt, Basra Oil Company liftings
Reserve replacement: WI 2P 679.6 mmboe (~16 years) and net-entitlement 1P only ~176 mmboe; the model's sustaining capex may be too low if replacement costs rise
Dividend above mid-cycle FCF, funded with ~9.9% USD debt: a payout cut is likely in the base case
Decommissioning obligations (HK$752m provision) could be under-provisioned for older Pakistan fields
Governance overhang: former Chairman Zhang Hong Wei's CSRC fine and lifetime ban, and a charging order over ~13.85% of shares held by an affiliated entity (per 0467.HK_Analysis.json)
